bull.b: TSMC’s high advanced-node mix demonstrates differentiated process technology, customer qualification, and manufacturing scale. This supports pricing power and reinforces its role in high-performance computing and AI, where leading-edge production is strategically important over multiple product cycles.

Strong expected revenue growth, supported by exceptionally robust AI demand, indicates a durable expansion opportunity rather than reliance on a single temporary product launch. Continued accelerator, networking, and agentic-AI adoption can sustain utilization and customer demand across several quarters.

Low and improving leverage gives TSMC financial flexibility while it funds large-scale technology and geographic expansion. Strong equity growth and high returns on equity indicate substantial earnings power, helping the company absorb investment demands without depending heavily on balance-sheet leverage.

bear.b: The overseas manufacturing build-out is strategically important but is expected to reduce gross margins as newer facilities ramp and operate below Taiwan’s scale advantages. If dilution reaches the guided 3%-4% range, it could structurally temper profitability even while capacity and geographic reach expand.

TSMC generates strong operating cash flow, but substantial fabrication and packaging investment limits the portion converted into free cash flow. Elevated reinvestment requirements can constrain discretionary cash, increase execution demands, and make shareholder returns more dependent on sustained demand and utilization.

TSMC’s exceptional profitability does not eliminate exposure to semiconductor cycles. Demand changes across smartphones, consumer electronics, and other end markets can produce uneven revenue and utilization, creating periods of weaker operating leverage even when the company retains strong long-term technology advantages.
